subject: Linguistics
title: Language Policy and Planning
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Language Policy and Planning.

hook.text: Singapore has four official languages. France legally protects French from English influence.

buildup.text: Language policy is a government's deliberate decisions about which languages to promote or restrict.

discovery.text: Policies cover education, courts, media, and signage—deciding who can use what language where.

twist.text: Even 'no policy' is a policy—it usually privileges the majority language by default.

climax.text: Language planning can revive endangered languages or suppress minority ones—it's inherently political.

punchline.text: Who decides which language matters is a question of power.

quiz.question: What does language policy determine?
options: Which languages are promoted or restricted
